hypotheses.justification: At `N = 0` the conclusion reads `(Gamma0 0).index * ∏ p ∈ (0:ℕ).primeFactors, p = 0 * ∏ p ∈ (0:ℕ).primeFactors, (p + 1)`. Since `Nat.primeFactors_zero : (0:ℕ).primeFactors = ∅` both products are `1`, so the goal is exactly `(Gamma0 0).index = 0` (the right-hand side is `0` whatever the second product is). This is true, so `hN` can be dropped: split on `N = 0`; the nonzero branch is the existing proof (`Gamma0_index_eq_prod_factorization hN` etc.), and the zero branch is the claim `(Gamma0 0).index = 0`, proved as follows. `Subgroup.index` is `Nat.card (SL(2,ℤ) ⧸ Gamma0 0)` (`Subgroup.index_eq_card`), so by `Subgroup.index_eq_zero_iff_infinite` it suffices that the quotient be infinite. By `mem_Gamma0_iff_dvd` (which the file states for every level, and which at level `0` says `A ∈ Gamma0 0 ↔ A 1 0 = 0`), `Gamma0 0` is the upper-triangular subgroup. The lower unipotent matrices `v n := ⟨!![1, 0; (n:ℤ), 1], by simp [det_fin_two_of]⟩` (the same construction as `lowerTriRep`, cf. lines 610–624) give pairwise distinct cosets: if `QuotientGroup.mk (v n) = QuotientGroup.mk (v m)`, then `QuotientGroup.eq_one_iff` yields `v n * (v m)⁻¹ ∈ Gamma0 0`, and `v n * (v m)⁻¹ = !![1, 0; (n:ℤ) - m, 1]` (an entry computation of the same shape as `lowerTriRep_diff_entry`), so `(0:ℤ) ∣ (n:ℤ) - m`, i.e. `n = m`. Hence `Infinite.of_injective` applied to `n ↦ QuotientGroup.mk (v n)` gives `Infinite (SL(2,ℤ) ⧸ Gamma0 0)` and the index is `0`. Note that no analogous deletion is possible for `Gamma0_index_eq_prod_factorization`: there the right-hand side at `N = 0` is the empty `Finsupp` product `1`, not `0`, so `hN` is genuinely needed in that companion statement; only the cleared-denominator form above is unconditional (matching Mathlib's unconditional `Nat.totient_mul_prod_primeFactors`).
